clues: This city grew along the banks of a calm river in the north east of Europe. Woods, lakes, and canals fill a full third of its land.
Winters here bite with frost, yet summers turn warm, a bigger swing than most sea side lands. Stone streets store heat, so nights stay warmer in town.
A wall split this city in two after a great war, and each half had its own rulers. In 1990 the halves joined, and it was a capital once more.
In 1990, artists from 21 lands painted bright murals on a long stretch of the old wall. That painted wall still stands, and crowds come to walk beside it.
All of Germany is governed from this city, the seat of its national parliament. That role came back in 1990, when the split land joined as one.
